# Presidents of the United States — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/us-presidents.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/us-presidents.ttl`](../decks/us-presidents.ttl) · **Cards:** 47 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

All 47 presidencies of the United States as of 4 October 2026, from George Washington (1st, 1789) to Donald Trump (47th, since 2025), numbered as the US government numbers them. Front: the number, e.g. "16th president of the United States"; back: the president's name in English and Swedish, with the years in office in a note. Grover Cleveland (22nd and 24th) and Donald Trump (45th and 47th) served non-consecutive terms and are counted twice, so the 47 presidencies were held by 45 people. Taken from Wikidata and checked against the Office of the Historian of the US House of Representatives, the White House, USA.gov and the Miller Center (University of Virginia).

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of presidencies, their numbers, the years in the notes and the English and Swedish names all come from it, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The House of Representatives' table, the White House and USA.gov (US government works, not under copyright in the US), the Miller Center (all rights reserved) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts that the Wikidata data gave, and no wording, table layout or selection was copied from them. The selection is the complete set of numbered presidencies, which any list of presidents shares because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from a list. The fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording of facts.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators; the library's process adds independent AI reviewers in later quality-control rounds. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. 1. Wikidata (query 1): every non-deprecated P39 (position held) statement whose value is President of the United States (Q11696), with its P1545 (series ordinal), P580 (start time) and P582 (end time) qualifiers, its rank and the English and Swedish labels, was fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service. The result also holds fictional presidents (characters from films, comics and television, among them "Quentin Trembley" with the ordinal "8½"), which have no numeric ordinal or are not humans. Query 2 therefore restricted the statements to those with a P1545 qualifier on items that are instances of human (P31 Q5) and fetched every English, Swedish and multilingual (mul) label and alias of those people. The rows with a whole-number ordinal are 47 statements, 1 to 47, on 45 items: Grover Cleveland (Q35171) holds two statements (22 and 24) and Donald Trump (Q22686) two (45 and 47, the latter of preferred rank and without an end time).
3. 2. Official US government check: the White House's former page listing all presidents (https://www.whitehouse.gov/about-the-white-house/presidents/) answered 404. USA.gov's page on the presidents (https://www.usa.gov/presidents, last updated March 2, 2026) states that Donald John Trump is the 47th and current president, sworn in on January 20, 2025, and links, for past presidents, to the table "Presidents, Vice Presidents, & Coinciding Sessions of Congress" of the House of Representatives' Office of the Historian. That table was downloaded (query 6) and parsed: it numbers 47 presidencies, Grover Cleveland as No. 22 and No. 24 and Donald J. Trump as No. 45 and No. 47 ("Jan. 20, 2025–present"). The White House's page on the current president (query 7) heads it "45th & 47th President of the United States".
4. 3. Independent check: the Miller Center of Public Affairs (University of Virginia) list of presidents (https://millercenter.org/president, query 8) gives a number, a first and last year and a name for each president. (Britannica's table of presidents was tried first and answered 403 to the research environment: curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o britannica.html -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{size_download}\n" https://www.britannica.com/topic/Presidents-of-the-United-States-1846696; it was not used.)
5. 4. Swedish: the Swedish Wikipedia list "Lista över USA:s presidenter" was fetched with its revision id through the MediaWiki API (query 9). Its rows link each president's Swedish article; every Swedish name on the cards is the Wikidata sv label (or, for George Washington, Ronald Reagan, George W. Bush, Barack Obama, Donald Trump and Joe Biden, who have no sv label, the mul label) and equals the title of the linked Swedish article. Its introduction uses the ordinal abbreviations "22:a och 24:e … 45:e och 47:e", the pattern used on the Swedish fronts: "USA:s 22:a president". The rule is Språkrådet's (Frågelådan, https://frageladan.isof.se/faqs/24030, query 12): a numeral, a colon and the last letter of the spelled-out ordinal ("1:a, 2:a, 3:e, 4:e och så vidare"). The Swedish ordinal abbreviation is therefore :a for numbers ending in 1 or 2 (första, andra, tjugoförsta …) except 11 and 12 (elfte, tolfte), and :e for all others.
6. 5. Cross-check: the script compare.py (query 10) parsed the saved Wikidata CSVs, the House table, the Miller Center list and the Swedish Wikipedia list, and compared for every number the first and last year in office; it found no disagreement. Its rules: Wikidata = the P39 statements of query 1 whose P1545 is a whole number, start and end year taken from P580 and P582 (no P582 = "present"); House table = the table rows grouped under each "No." (a row with an empty No. cell continues the presidency above), start year from the first row's dates of service and end year from the last row's ("present" if it has none); Miller Center = the "president-number", "inauguration-date" and "date-ended" fields of each entry (the end year is not compared where Wikidata has no end); Swedish Wikipedia = the last four characters of "tillträde" and "frånträde" in the {{Tabell befattningshavare}} block with that "nummer" (wiki links and <ref> notes removed). The script compares years only; that each number belongs to the same person in every source, and the name forms, were checked by reading the parsed rows side by side. The script wrote its parsed readings to compare.json, and the evidence on every card (the "says" texts of the Wikidata, House, Miller Center and Swedish Wikipedia evidence) was generated from those parsed fields by make_dossier.py, not typed by hand; the readings of the White House and USA.gov pages were added by hand. The scripts themselves are not published with the deck; the rules above are what they do. The Miller Center's end year for the current term, which the script does not compare (Wikidata has no end), was read by hand: it is an error on that page (see quality control). The names were compared by reading: the House table uses formal forms ("William H. Taft", "Richard M. Nixon", "Gerald R. Ford", "James Earl “Jimmy” Carter", "William J. Clinton", "Donald J. Trump", "Joseph R. Biden Jr."), the Miller Center "William Harrison" and "William Taft"; all name the same person as the Wikidata item. The cards use the Wikidata English label, the name by which each president is commonly known, except for Franklin D. Roosevelt, whose English label is the full "Franklin Delano Roosevelt": the card uses "Franklin D. Roosevelt" (an English and a mul alias of the item, the form of the House table, the Miller Center and the Swedish label).
7. 6. Cards: front "<ordinal> president of the United States" / "USA:s <ordinal> president" (English ordinals 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 21st …); back: the name; back note: "President <first year>–<last year>" in both languages, from the years of the P580 and P582 qualifiers, with the months for the two presidencies that began and ended in the same year (William Henry Harrison and James A. Garfield); the notes do not say how a presidency ended (death, assassination or resignation), so that no card implies anything about the others, and, for Cleveland and Trump, the other number and term. Study direction front to back only, because Cleveland and Trump each answer two cards.
8. 7. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the item holds P39 Q11696 and has the English and Swedish name of the back as a label or alias (in that language or mul). The builder's checks therefore confirm only that each person held the office and the English and Swedish name forms; they would not notice two cards with their names swapped. The number on each front and the years in each note are qualifiers of the P39 statement, which the builder's checks cannot reach; they rest on query 1 and the comparison in step 5 (Wikidata, the House table, the Miller Center and the Swedish Wikipedia) and are recorded in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

Every presidency of the United States from the first (George Washington, 1789) to the current one (Donald Trump's second term, since 20 January 2025), as of 4 October 2026: 47 cards. A presidency is a numbered term of continuous service, the convention of the US government (the House of Representatives' table, the White House, USA.gov), of Wikidata and of the Miller Center: a president who served two non-consecutive terms is counted twice, so Grover Cleveland is the 22nd and the 24th president and Donald Trump the 45th and the 47th, and the 47 presidencies were held by 45 people. Consecutive terms of the same president are one presidency (Franklin D. Roosevelt's four terms are the 32nd). Left out: acting presidents and anyone who exercised the powers of the office temporarily under the 25th Amendment (not numbered by any source), vice presidents, presidents of the Continental Congress or under the Articles of Confederation (before the Constitution) and the Confederate States, and the fictional presidents that the Wikidata query also returned. The current presidency is the cut-off: the note says "since 2025".

## Queries

**1. Every P39 statement for President of the United States with ordinal, start, end, rank and labels (sh q1.sh, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > q1.csv)** (Wikidata: the holders of the position President of the United States (Q11696), with the series ordinal, start and end of each term and the English and Swedish labels and aliases of the presidents)

```
SELECT ?person ?en ?sv ?ordinal ?start ?end ?rank WHERE {
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 wd:Q11696 ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  FILTER(?rank != wikibase:DeprecatedRank)
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1545 ?ordinal }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?start

```

**2. English, Swedish and mul labels and aliases of the human holders with an ordinal (sh run.sh q2, the same curl command with q2.rq)** (Wikidata: the holders of the position President of the United States (Q11696), with the series ordinal, start and end of each term and the English and Swedish labels and aliases of the presidents)

```
SELECT ?person ?ordinal ?kind ?lang ?text WHERE {
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 wd:Q11696 ; pq:P1545 ?ordinal .
  ?person wdt:P31 wd:Q5 .
  { ?person rdfs:label ?text . BIND("label" AS ?kind) }
  UNION { ?person skos:altLabel ?text . BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  BIND(LANG(?text) AS ?lang)
  FILTER(?lang IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
ORDER BY xsd:integer(?ordinal) ?lang ?kind

```


## Quality control

5 rounds, 23 findings: 14 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 8 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (141 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's number, name and years against Wikidata, the House of Representatives' table, the Miller Center and the Swedish Wikipedia; the current president against the White House and USA.gov; the Swedish names and ordinals against Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish Wikipedia. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 47 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata, the House table, the Miller Center and the Swedish Wikipedia agree on the number, the person and the first and last year of all 47 presidencies, and the White House and USA.gov confirm that Donald Trump is the 47th and current president. No Wikidata check was skipped. The differences found are in name forms, in Wikidata's modelling (fictional presidents, missing sv labels) and one error on the Miller Center page; none affects a card.

Recorded in the card's evidence. | no change needed |

Two suggestions, both applied: the death-in-office remark on William Henry Harrison's card only was removed, and the method now says plainly what the builder's Wikidata checks do and do not cover.
